To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inkjet printing is a promising technique for the fabrication of organic thin film transistors.

we have successfully optimized the inkjet-printed pentacene devices by using photolithography-defined patterns and that the optimized devices show the highest performance among inkjet-printed devices reported to date.
we have demonstrated the first use of photolithography to define the geometry and dimensions of inkjet-printed organic semiconductors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of inkjet printing techniques for the fabrication of organic field effect transistors.
the development of a simple, cost-effective, high-throughput, and low-temperature method for the fabrication of high-quality organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs).
the fabrication and characterization of inkjet-printed organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inkjet-printed pentacene devices are comparable to the devices made from thermally evaporated films.

the optimization of the inkjet-printed PTE-PTC devices is a complex task, which is not only dependent on the ink composition but also on the printing parameters, the substrate properties and the post-processing steps.

the optimization of the inkjet-printed 6, 13-bis(triisopro-pylsilylethyny) pentacene (TIPS-PEN) using photolithography-defined structures has resulted in a significant improvement in device performance and reproducibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for inkjet printing of organic semiconductors with the ability to produce devices with high performance and reproducibility, which are comparable with the best results reported in the literature.
we developed a new ink for printing organic semiconductors and demonstrated that the printed organic semiconductor can be used in a transistor.
we have demonstrated that photolithographically defined patterns are useful in the optimization process of inkjet-printed organic semiconductors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inkjet printing is not only capable of producing high-quality, high-resolution organic electronic devices, but it is also capable of producing high-resolution organic electronic structures.
inkjet printing of organic semiconductors can be used to make devices that have comparable performance to those made with conventional solution processing techniques.
photolithography is a powerful tool for studying and improving the performance of inkjet-printed organic thin-film transistors (TFTs).
